To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

indeterminate sentences are resolved through pragmatic inferences that involve the left and right inferior frontal gyruses, the left and right superior temporal gyrus, and the anterior cignulate cortex.

(1) the brain processes indeterminate sentences in a different manner than it does control sentences; and (2) the brain processes anomalous sentences differently than it processes indeterminate sentences.

the brain regions that are involved in the processing of indeterminate sentences include the superior temporal gyruses bilaterally, the anterior cingulated cortex, and the inferior frontal gyri bilaterally.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of the interpretation of indeterminate sentences.
the cognitive processes that underpin sentence comprehension and their neural correlates.

the cognitive and neural correlates of sentence processing and, more specifically, the role that the brain plays in the comprehension of sentences that require the use of pragmatic inferences to enrich their semantic composition.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural correlates of indeterminate sentence comprehension are more likely to involve the deployment of pragmatic processes, rather than of semantic ones.
the neuroanatomically distributed network for the comprehension of indeterminate sentences is a function of the type and nature of the pragmatic inferences that are required to resolve the sentence.
indeterminate sentences are processed in a distributed network, with the STG, R-IFG and ACC playing a central role in the resolution of the ambiguity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain regions involved in the comprehension of indeterminate sentences are not limited to the vmPFC and L-IFG but include a number of other brain areas that may play a role in the resolution of semantic underspecification in language.
the neural correlates of indeterminate sentence comprehension are more complex than previously reported.
pragmatic inferences are not limited to the resolution of indeterminacy but are more broadly involved in the comprehension of natural language.
The main takeaway from our work is that
indeterminate sentences are resolved via pragmatic processes, not via semantic coercion.
indeterminate sentence comprehension involves the recruitment of multiple brain areas, which may reflect the complexity of the pragmatic-inferential process involved.
the neurocognitive processes that support indeterminacy resolution are not restricted to the vmPFC or the L-IFG but are distributed across the whole brain.
